bib.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

question: Can diffusion models be trained and sampled at far lower compute, while keeping quality, by running them in the latent space of a pretrained perceptual autoencoder?
hypothesis: Splitting perceptual compression (autoencoder) from semantic generation (diffusion) with only mild downsampling (f=4-8) reaches a near-optimal complexity/detail trade-off.
contributions: Scales better to high-dimensional data than transformer-based two-stage approaches; mild compression gives more faithful reconstructions and megapixel synthesis
Competitive results on unconditional synthesis, inpainting, stochastic super-resolution at much lower compute, including lower inference cost
No delicate weighting of reconstruction vs generative loss (unlike LSGM); little latent regularization
Convolutional application to densely conditioned tasks, ~1024^2 px images
General cross-attention conditioning for class, text and layout-to-image
Release of pretrained latent diffusion and autoencoding models

method.summary: Stage 1 trains an adversarial+perceptual autoencoder (KL- or VQ-regularized, downsampling f) once. Stage 2 trains a time-conditional UNet diffusion model with epsilon-prediction loss in the latent space, with domain encoders tau_theta feeding cross-attention (or channel concatenation for spatial conditions).
method.task: image synthesis (unconditional, class/text/layout/semantic-map conditional, super-resolution, inpainting)

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.split: class-conditional 256x256; SR follows SR3 pipeline (images with shorter side <256 removed), eval on validation split
datasets.preprocessing: SR low-res via bicubic interpolation with anti-aliasing

datasets.name: MS-COCO
datasets.size: 30000 val samples for FID/IS (text-to-image); 2048 unaugmented COCO-Stuff challenge-split examples for layout FID

datasets.name: OpenImages
datasets.split: autoencoder zoo trained here; layout-to-image trained here then finetuned on COCO; layout eval 2048 center-cropped val images

datasets.name: Places
datasets.split: train on random 256x256 crops, test on 512x512 crops

datasets.name: Flickr-Landscapes with semantic maps
datasets.preprocessing: downsampled semantic maps concatenated with latent

models.name: Autoencoder (KL or VQ-reg), e.g. f=4 |Z|=8192 c=3
models.architecture: convolutional encoder/decoder, patch-based discriminator; VQ layer absorbed into decoder

models.name: LDM UNet (ablated UNet from ADM, self-attn replaced by transformer blocks with cross-attn)
models.params: 169M to 1.45B (Table 15): text-to-image 1.45B, class ImageNet LDM-4 395M, LDM-4 inpainting 215M, SR 169M, uncond LSUN/FFHQ/CelebA 274M
models.architecture: time-conditional UNet, 1000 diffusion steps, linear noise schedule
models.init_from: trained from scratch on frozen first-stage latents
models.layers: Depth 2 (UNet); text transformer tau_theta depth N=32

models.name: Baselines: ADM/ADM-G, SR3, LaMa, StyleGAN2, ProjectedGAN, BigGAN-deep, GLIDE, Make-A-Scene, CogView, VQGAN+T

training.objective: L_LDM = E[||eps - eps_theta(z_t,t,tau_theta(y))||^2] (Eq 3); autoencoder: reconstruction (perceptual) + adversarial + small KL/VQ reg (Eq 25)
training.lr: per model, 1e-6 to 1.3e-4 (Tables 12-15); text-to-image 1.0e-4, ImageNet LDM-4 1.0e-4, inpainting 1.0e-6 (as printed)
training.batch_size: per model: text-to-image 680, class ImageNet LDM-4 1200, LDM-8 64, SR 64, inpainting 128, layout COCO 48, landscapes 48 (Table 15)
training.steps: text-to-image 390K; class LDM-4 178K; LDM-8 2.9M-4.8M; SR 860K; inpainting 360K; analysis runs 2M (ImageNet) / 500k (CelebA); CelebA-HQ 410k, FFHQ 635k, Churches 500k, Bedrooms 1.9M
training.dropout: 0.1 for the layout-to-image COCO row only
training.regularisation: autoencoder KL weight ~1e-6 or VQ codebook; latent rescaled by component-wise std from first batch for KL spaces
training.hardware: single NVIDIA A100 for all models except inpainting (eight V100)
training.compute: Table 18, in V100-days (A100 days x2.2): LDM-4-G ImageNet 271; LDM-8-G 91 overall; LSUN-Bedrooms LDM-4 60; CelebA-HQ 14.4; FFHQ 26; LSUN-Churches LDM-8 18

other.learning_rates_maximised: learning rates were maximised per model while still stable, so they vary between runs
other.best_checkpoint: CelebA analysis: best checkpoint used if converged before 500k

inference.decoding: DDIM sampler, 10-500 steps depending on experiment; classifier-free guidance for ImageNet and text-to-image
inference.samples: 50k samples for FID/Precision/Recall (Tables 1, 10); 30000 for COCO text-to-image; 5k for efficiency plots (Fig 6, 7, 17)
inference.prompting: text prompt via BERT tokenizer into transformer tau_theta, cross-attention

parameters.imagenet_table3: 250 DDIM steps, cfg s=1.5 (also 1.25 in Table 10)
parameters.convolutional_sampling: model trained at 256^2 applied convolutionally to 512^2-1024^2

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet inception distance via torch-fidelity, cross-checked with Dhariwal & Nichol script (7.76 vs 7.77 on ImageNet; 2.95 vs 3.0 on Bedrooms)

metrics.name: R-FID
metrics.definition: reconstruction FID of autoencoder vs ImageNet-val

metrics.name: Precision/Recall
metrics.definition: Kynkaanniemi et al. via Dhariwal & Nichol script

eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds or confidence intervals reported except +/- on IS and per-image std for PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS. FID on 50k samples for headline tables, 5k for efficiency plots.

availability.weights: pretrained latent diffusion and autoencoding models released at same URL

prompts.text: Which of the two images is a better high quality version of the low resolution image in the middle?
Which of the two images contains more realistic inpainted regions of the image in the middle?

evidence.quote: All models trained on a single NVIDIA A100 except for the inpainting model which was trained on eight V100.

results.claim: Class-conditional ImageNet LDM-4 with classifier-free guidance reaches FID 3.60 at 400M parameters, beating ADM-G (4.59, 608M).
results.setup: ImageNet 256x256 class-conditional, LDM-4-G, 250 DDIM steps, cfg scale 1.5, 178K train steps, batch 1200
results.note: Table 10 also lists 3.95 at cfg scale 1.25.

results.claim: LDM-8 beats pixel-based LDM-1 by an FID gap of 38 after 2M training steps on class-conditional ImageNet under equal compute.
results.setup: Class-conditional ImageNet, single A100, same steps and parameter count, 100 DDIM steps, FID on 5k samples
results.quote: niﬁcant FID [29] gap of 38 between pixel-based diffusion
results.note: Source text has a ligature: 'significant FID [29] gap of 38 between pixel-based diffusion (LDM-1) and LDM-8 after 2M training steps'.

results.claim: Unconditional CelebA-HQ 256x256 LDM-4 sets FID 5.11 (500 DDIM steps), reported as new state of the art over likelihood-based models and GANs.
results.quote: On CelebA-HQ, we report a new state-of-the-art FID of 5.11
results.note: Table 1 lists ProjectedGAN 3.08 for FFHQ, not CelebA-HQ; 200-step LDM-4 is 4.98 on CelebA-HQ in the table (and FFHQ 4.98 in Table 18).

results.claim: Latent inpainting gives at least 2.7x speed-up and at least 1.6x better FID than pixel-based diffusion at fixed parameters.
results.setup: Places inpainting, LDM-1 (pixel) vs LDM-4, FID after six epochs, same parameter count
results.quote: we observe a speed-up of at least 2.7× between pixel- and latent-based diffusion models
results.note: FID improvement factor 1.6x stated in same sentence.

results.claim: Big inpainting LDM-4 with 512 fine-tuning reaches FID 1.50 on all samples, vs LaMa 2.23 (recomputed).
results.setup: Places, 30k crops of 512x512, LDM-4 big w/ ft
results.table: Table 7, row LDM-4 (ours, big, w/ ft), column All samples FID

results.claim: Text-to-image 1.45B LDM-KL-8-G reaches zero-shot MS-COCO FID 12.63 with classifier-free guidance s=1.5, versus 23.31 unguided.
results.setup: LAION-400M-trained 1.45B model, MS-COCO 256x256 val, 30000 samples, 250 DDIM steps

results.claim: Autoencoder f=4 (8192 codes, c=3) reconstructs ImageNet-val at R-FID 0.58 and PSNR 27.43, vs DALL-E f=8 R-FID 32.01 and VQGAN f=16 4.98.
results.setup: Autoencoders trained on OpenImages, evaluated on ImageNet-Val

results.claim: LDM-4 for 4x super-resolution reaches FID 2.8 (val features) / 4.8 (train features) vs SR3 5.2, but lower PSNR 24.4 vs 26.4 and IS 166.3 vs 180.1.
results.table: Table 5, row LDM-4 (ours, 100 steps), column FID
results.note: Image regression gets highest PSNR 27.9 and SSIM 0.801.

results.claim: Compute: LDM-4-G ImageNet uses 271 V100-days training vs 962 for ADM-G; LSUN-Bedrooms LDM-4 60 vs ADM 232 V100-days.
results.setup: A100 days converted to V100 days with an assumed x2.2 speedup
results.table: Table 18, row LDM-4-G (ours, 250 ddim steps 178K...), column Overall Compute

results.claim: User study: humans prefer LDM-4 over pixel-DM (70.6% vs 29.4%) for super-resolution and over LaMa (68.1% vs 31.9%) for inpainting in head-to-head choice.
results.setup: 2-alternative forced choice following SR3, 3 s viewing; sample size of raters not stated
results.table: Table 4, row Task 2: Preference Score, column LDM-4 (SR)
results.note: Task 1 preference vs ground truth: 30.4% (LDM-4) vs 16.0% (Pixel-DM); inpainting 21.0% vs 13.6%.

results.claim: LDM-4 and LDM-8 give the best balance; LDM-1/2 train slowly and LDM-32 stalls from too much compression.
results.setup: Class-conditional ImageNet, f in {1,2,4,8,16,32}, 2M steps, single A100
results.quote: In summary, LDM-4 and -8 offer the best conditions for achieving high-quality synthesis results.

limits: Sequential sampling is still slower than GANs (authors).
Autoencoder reconstruction can bottleneck tasks needing pixel-level precision; super-resolution assumed to be affected (authors).
Optimizer, warmup, schedule, precision and seeds not stated; single runs.
Learning rates differ per model in the f-comparison (maximised per model), a confound the authors note.
Compute comparison to ADM uses an assumed x2.2 A100-to-V100 conversion and numbers copied from Dhariwal & Nichol.
Bicubic-trained SR does not generalize to other degradations; needed LDM-BSR.
Societal: deepfakes, training-data leakage, bias amplification (authors).
